newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Court ruling makes Sydney tobacconists fume.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Court ruling makes Sydney tobacconists fume.

text.p: Sydney tobacco retailers expressed fear for their livelihoods on Thursday after a court ruling that the inside of a tobacconist's shop was a public place and could not therefore display cigarette advertising.

The New South Wales Supreme Court on Wednesday dismissed an appeal by a Sydney tobacconist against a lower court decision that tobacco adverts in his shop breached a state law banning cigarette advertising in public places.

Jim Phillbrook, executive director of the NSW Retail Tobacco Traders' Association, said the ruling had heavy implications for the New South Wales' 800 tobacconists and thousands of other small retailers.
If the ruling was imposed, shops might not even be able to display the price of cigarettes or might even have to stock them under the counter.
"A lot of these tobacconists only exist by being price-cutters," he said. "If they can't feature prices as they are doing now, then they'll go out of business."
Phillbrook added: "I've had retailers ringing me all morning asking what they're going to do."
Australia, and New South Wales in particular, already has strong U.S.-style anti-smoking legislation that has seen the number of smokers decline steadily.
The federal and state governments earn an estimated A$4.5 billion a year in taxes on tobacco products, Phillbrook said.
